arguments.content: There is no such integer. A perfect square cannot be a prime number because any perfect square n = k^2 (where k > 1) has factors 1, k, and k^2, making it a composite number, and 1 is not prime.

I have written the answer to `answer.txt`.

There is no such integer. By definition, a perfect square greater than 1 has at least three distinct positive divisors (1, its square root, and itself), so it cannot be a prime number. 1 is not considered a prime number either (it only has one divisor). Therefore, a perfect square can never be a prime number.
